control.devtoolsEndpoint hands the engine's DevTools port, token and generation only to a connection the control socket admitted (peer UID, then on macOS the bundled ardia, Team-signed code or a doorbell approval; same-user test instances as for every method). Native checks again on the socket queue, before and after reading, that the connection is still open and its approval live (ControlSocket.admits), drops any reply to a connection whose approval ran out (ControlSocket.reply), and checks the approval again before the writer starts each line (ControlConnection mayWrite), so a line queued behind a slow reader never starts after the approval ends. The token is read from the engine's dedicated ac_cli_devtools_endpoint call when the engine has it (callForSecretReply, bytes wiped), never from the shared ac_cli_control status, else from ArdiaControl.json opened O_NOFOLLOW, required a regular file of the user's with no group or other bits and no access list letting others in (PrivateFolder.privateFile), at most 64 KiB, whose port, generation and pid match the running server (DevtoolsEndpoint.read); it must be 16 to 256 base64url characters. Refused while control is off, at arrival and again after the read; turning control off cuts native off synchronously (ControlSocket.cutOff, one lock shared by the writer, replies, admission and the token read) before the asynchronous stop; where the socket has no doorbell (Linux, Windows) the method is unlisted and answers unknown_method. In JS it is a Secret of kind devtoolsToken from the moment it arrives (platform/automation.ts) and is revealed only on that one reply line (socketDevtools.devtoolsEndpointLine). Swift tests in packages/shell/controlpeer-tests, JS in socketDevtools.test.mjs (the shared hostile-input corpus as params, param names, own prototype keys and request ids, checked at the native read and the reply line) and secretContainment.test.mjs

Engine token server: loopback only; before the token is read, anything a browser sends (Origin, Sec-Fetch-Site, Sec-Fetch-Dest) or a Host other than 127.0.0.1:<port> or localhost:<port> is refused (ArdiaRequestIsFromProgram), so no page, extension, service worker or DNS-rebound name in a browser that sends Fetch Metadata (Chromium, Firefox 90+, Safari 16.4+) reaches it, and an older Safari top-level GET still needs the token and can't read the answer; a 32-byte token compared in constant time (ControlServer::Accepts) from the 0600 ArdiaControl.json, published through one open descriptor of a folder no other user owns or can write, with no macOS access list naming anyone but you and not on a volume that ignores ownership (UnsafeControlFolder), the file stripped of inherited ACLs and checked 0600 (OnlyOwnerCanRead); RemoteDebuggingAllowed policy; then a full DevTools client by the owner's decision (#2807). TokenClient::FilterCommand keeps only framing: a JSON object with an integer id and string method, params an object, a known sessionId, one command per (session, id), 4096 waiting replies at most

Ardia.consoleDelta, Ardia.focusedFrameOrigin and Ardia.hitTest are answered by the engine, not the page: TokenClient::StartPageSignal takes them only after FilterCommand's framing checks and only on a session this client attached to a page or tab target, so they pass the same inspection gate as that attach (Chrome's DevTools availability policy and the frame checks in ShouldAllowSession); the browser session, an iframe's session and any targetId are refused, and RunPageSignal checks IsInspectionAllowed for the tab again at answer time (ContentsInspectable), the focused frame's own policy before reading its origin, and the ring withholds entries from frames the policy keeps from inspection (FrameInspectable). RunPageSignal refuses any parameter it doesn't know (UnknownParam), takes after, generation and limit only as whole numbers in range (WholeNumber), x and y only as finite numbers within a million CSS pixels (Coordinate), backendNodeId only as a positive integer, and expectedOrigin only as a bare http or https origin that serializes back to itself (the hostile corpus caught chrome:// and chrome-untrusted:// origins getting through before); the focused frame's origin and document id come from the browser's own RenderFrameHost, never from the page; the hit test's DevTools answers are parsed field by field with types checked, its ancestor walk runs in an isolated world the page can't reach, at most 32 ancestors, node names cut to 64 characters, a 3 second deadline, at most 4 probes at once, refused for a frame at the point the policy keeps from inspection (FrameInspectable), re-run when the page scrolled between reading the scroll position and hit-testing, cancelled when the session detaches or the client goes (teardown deferred to a later task) and stopped when the page or the hit frame navigates, and a cross-site iframe is reported as a remote frame rather than a blocker; console text the ring keeps is sliced in UTF-16 before conversion and cut to 2048 bytes and source URLs to 512 at a UTF-8 boundary, at most 200 entries per tab, with a generation so a replaced ring reads as reset. Replies go back only to the asking connection while its session is still attached. Windows WebUI host (--ardia-shell=webui): webui_updates.cc fetches windows-update.json (at most 64 KiB) and windows-update.json.sig (exactly 64 bytes) through Chromium's system URLLoaderFactory with credentials omitted and the cache off, only from the GitHub windows-alpha release (or, in a test instance only, an ARDIA_INSTANCE updateFeed that ValidFeedUrl accepts: https, or http to 127.0.0.1, localhost or 10.0.2.2), and follows a redirect only to https on port 443 at github.com, objects.githubusercontent.com or release-assets.githubusercontent.com for the release feed and never for a test feed (AllowedRedirect); while holding the Updates folder and a fresh scratch folder inside it open without delete sharing, it creates each file with CREATE_NEW, no sharing and FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT, checks its final path (GetFinalPathNameByHandleW) is a direct child and it has one link before writing, then reopens it read-only with only FILE_SHARE_READ, checks it is the same file (volume and file index) with the bytes it wrote, and holds that handle while it runs the bundled ardia-update-verify.exe windows-manifest against the pinned windows-update.pem beside Ardia.exe (a test key only in a test instance) with a 15 s deadline and only its own pipe and NUL inherited; ReadVerifierAnswer takes only its last line, an ok line of exactly five words whose version, build above Ardia.build.json's, URL under the published prefix (ValidInstallerUrl), lowercase SHA-256 and size up to 1 GiB all pass, and keeps the verified offer and its signed bytes in the browser process: the renderer never sends a URL, hash or path. The installer streams (SimpleURLLoader DownloadAsStream) into a staging file with an unpredictable name (StagingFileName, Ardia-Setup-<sha16>-<random 64 bits>.part) created the same way and held with no sharing, capped at the signed size and hashed as it is written; it is renamed through that handle (FileRenameInfo), reopened with only FILE_READ_DATA, FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES and SYNCHRONIZE (never DELETE, so CreateProcessW can open the image) and only FILE_SHARE_READ (kHeldInstallerAccess, kHeldInstallerShare, HeldInstallerLetsItRun), checked to be the same file (volume and file index) with the signed size and SHA-256, and that handle is held through ardia-update-verify.exe windows-package and until CreateProcessW on Restart to Update (InstallerSink), so no other writer can change it in between; one install at a time is reserved on the UI sequence (BeginInstall), a second Restart from any window gets busy, and a background instance never runs it. A file that fails a check is deleted only through the handle Ardia created or verified (FileDispositionInfo), never by path, and one whose identity can't be confirmed is left alone; a failed launch releases the held installer. Automatic checks run only when the app-data folder is the production one (ScratchDataDirectory), so a scratch ARDIA_DATA_DIR instance never checks unless a test instance names updateFeed. scripts/windows/engine/tests/webui_update_policy_test.cc unit-tests the pure policy, and apps/browser/src/hostileInputs.test.mjs compiles it and pipes the whole shared hostile list through every verifier answer field and line, asserting that only valid offers ever pass BeginDownload and BeginInstall, with a valid control

rows.guard: Windows WebUI host (--ardia-shell=webui): ArdiaUpdates.installKind, status, check, update, claimOutcome and restart run only for the live trusted chrome://ardia/ shell document; every call goes through the pure CheckUpdateCall in webui_update_policy.h before it reaches the service: an args value that is present but not a list is refused, installKind, status, check and restart take no arguments, update takes one whole build number from 1 to 2^53-1 (BuildArgument), starts only when it is the build the last verified check offered and the copy is installed (BeginDownload), and says whether this call started the run, so only the window that started it records the consent period, claimOutcome takes one whole run number (RunArgument) and answers with the outcome it consumed, so a window counts and shows only that, anything else is refused with an error; the renderer reads every reply through readEngineStatus and readCheckAnswer in apps/desktop/src/platform/win/hostUpdates.ts, which keep only known phases and kinds, map any reason outside the engine's own set to other, drop an offer unless it is newer than the running build, versions matching ^[0-9][0-9A-Za-z.+-]{0,63}$, safe integer builds above the running build and sizes up to 1 GiB, and messages of at most 200 characters without control characters; apps/browser/src/hostileInputs.test.mjs compiles webui_update_policy_test and sends every shared hostile value, after the same JSON round trip the bridge makes, as each call's only argument, beside a second argument and as the whole args value, asserting that only whole numbers in range ever pass and that none but the valid controls reach BeginDownload or ClaimOutcome; apps/desktop/src/platform/win/hostUpdates.test.mjs runs the shared hostile list through both readers and the saved preferences
checks: apps/desktop/src/platform/win/hostUpdates.test.mjs#windows webui update replies refuse every hostile input
apps/browser/src/hostileInputs.test.mjs#windows webui native update policy keeps every hostile input and call argument away

rows.guard: Rust Netscape HTML bookmarks parser behind libardia_import, not linked by any host yet: a file over 64 MiB is refused before it is read, 64 folder levels and 250,000 nodes with each folder reserved before its contents, no recursion on the input, and one slot per attribute the parser reads whatever a tag carries; entities decode once and titles and URLs reach the tree verbatim, place: queries are skipped and scheme policy stays with import:bookmarks; the shared hostile list runs through the static library
Fixed schema of settings and catalog pins; values checked by updateSettings (C7: preview after apply)
ARDIA_FEEDBACK_URL and debug-port flags honoured by the launch config (D8, D9)

WebKit's page menu sends the link, image or media address the page holds as an app-wide event with a native request number; only a non-empty string with an integer request is passed on, after cleanUrlReport strips tracking parameters, and native writes it only for its latest request while the pasteboard is unchanged since that menu action

The app's own renderer child processes only (proc_listpids by parent pid, extension renderers left out), read with proc_pid_rusage on a background queue; a pid whose parent or start time changed during the read is dropped. JS takes only rows whose pid, start time and CPU time are finite non-negative numbers (validReadings); readings of a reused pid or more than 25 s apart start over

Windows WebUI host (--ardia-shell=webui): ardiaRequest is taken only from the shell WebContents' live primary main frame whose committed origin is chrome://ardia/, by the handler bound to that document's generation; a new document (reload or renderer swap) or a renderer exit retires the generation, dropping its pending replies, events and pages, and a page asked for by a retired document is never created and its profile never loaded; OnJavascriptDisallowed drops that handler's pending replies at once and retires the generation only if the handler no longer owns the live document; requests of the wrong shape are dropped; tab URLs pass AllowedPageUrl before any profile loads and before each navigation, refusing javascript:, chrome://ardia in any spelling or behind view-source:, non-text URLs and anything unparsable; private profiles are refused; scripts/windows/webui-pilot/bridge.ps1 sends the hostile cases at the sinks in a Windows guest Each Chromium browser window carries its own ShellHostView over its BrowserView, and a bridge answers only the host whose shell WebContents it was created for (WindowRegistry::HostForShell), so one window's shell document cannot drive another window; tab.create, tab.viewport, tab.command, tab.release, tab.presentations and tab.close act only on a tab whose numeric id and non-empty claim match a binding this window holds (ClaimedBinding), keys and claims are 1-256 bytes without control characters (ValidTabKey, ValidClaim), viewport and input-region rectangles must be finite, non-negative in size and within +/-1e6 (ValidRect), an adoptId is only tab:<1..INT_MAX> naming an unbound tab in one of this window's own browsers with the requested profile (ParseAdoptId), a key held by another window moves only after that window marked it transferable and only within the same profile, and scripts/windows/engine/tests/webui_window_policy_test.cc unit-tests these validators.

Windows WebUI host (--ardia-shell=webui): ArdiaShell.readDocument, writeDocument, saveDocument and removeDocument run only for the live trusted chrome://ardia/ shell document; document names must pass ValidWindowsDocumentName (1-200 [A-Za-z0-9._-], matching ardia-shell-migration's DOCUMENT_NAME_LIMIT, no path separators, colons/ADS, control chars, .., leading/trailing dots or spaces, or Windows reserved device names CON/PRN/AUX/NUL/COM0-9/LPT0-9) and must not be reserved (session.json, live.json, live.canonical.json, rnw-migration.json, rnw-migration.lock, launch-starts.txt, launch-starts.txt.tmp, window-placement.txt, case-insensitive), and writes and removes also refuse the engine-owned launch-guard.json in any case (WritableWindowsDocumentName) while reads and bootstrap.documents keep it for launch telemetry; writes are capped at WindowsDocumentLimit (8 MiB, 48 MiB for sync-state.nns in any letter case) and reads at kWindowsDocumentReadLimit (64 MiB, the migrator's DOCUMENT_LIMIT); reads, writes and deletes open the destination directory and target handles with FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT, refuse directories/devices/reparse points and multiply-linked files (nNumberOfLinks != 1), verify final-path direct-child containment inside the app-data directory's canonical final path (the root is opened following reparse points, so the root itself may be a junction; every document file is opened with FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT) via GetFinalPathNameByHandleW and IsDirectChildOfWinDirectory, validate UTF-8 on reads (base::IsStringUTF8), stage writes through a CREATE_NEW handle committed handle-relatively via NtSetInformationFile (FileRenameInformationEx fallback FileRenameInformation with held RootDirectory handle and leaf name only) and delete via FileDispositionInformationEx/FileDispositionInfo on the open handle; bootstrap.documents enumerates only eligible non-reparse single-link valid-UTF-8 regular files bounded by count and total bytes (BootstrapDocumentFits, checked against the listed size before a file is opened and again after the read) and reaches the page through JSON.parse (BootstrapAssignmentScript), so a document named __proto__ stays an own property; ReadAsset verifies regular single-link non-reparse disk files and strict final-path containment inside AssetDirectory() via IsStrictlyWithinWinDirectory; scripts/windows/webui-pilot/bridge.ps1 runs the shared hostile corpus against the document sinks, requiring the exact native ERR_DOCUMENT_REQUEST/ERR_DOCUMENT_NAME code for refused values (a synchronous throw, transport error or timeout fails) and a confined write/read/remove round trip for names the policy accepts (prototype keys, "1", "true") with Object.prototype unchanged, plus reparse-point escape checks (ERR_DOCUMENT_READ/WRITE/REMOVE) and a reload proving a __proto__ document survives in bootstrap.documents, scripts/windows/webui-pilot/junction.ps1 proves junction escapes out of ardia-ui are refused with a CSP-allowed image control and sends the shared hostile corpus raw and URL-encoded through chrome://ardia/ checking each request against ArdiaShell.testAssetSink (counted only in a test instance): a same-origin request moves exactly one of served/refused/outsideRoot/unreadable and never served or outsideRoot, a cross-origin one moves none, and values the URL parser resolves to the shell page are counted and not sent, final paths are compared case-sensitively after the drive letter or UNC share (WinFinalPathStartsWith), and scripts/windows/engine/tests/webui_policy_test.cc unit-tests the pure validators The engine's own live.canonical.json and window-placement.txt go through ReadDocumentFile and WriteDocumentFile, the same handle-checked I/O without the reserved-name refusal, and are never named by a page request.

Windows WebUI host (--ardia-shell=webui): ArdiaTelemetry.post runs only for the live trusted chrome://ardia/ shell document, requires exactly two string arguments passing TelemetryPostAllowed (ardia::desktop_telemetry_policy::PostAcceptable: a non-empty body <= 512 KiB starting with { and an ak_<kind>_<24 hex> ingest key with no header-injection bytes; then base::JSONReader in RFC mode must parse the body as a JSON object), caps concurrent in-flight requests at kMaxInFlight, posts only to the hardcoded kEndpoint (in a test instance only, ARDIA_TEST_TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT may name an http localhost URL instead) through Chromium's system URLLoaderFactory with CredentialsMode::kOmit, RedirectMode::kError and LOAD_DISABLE_CACHE, cancels in-flight posts on TearDown, and replies only with the filtered HTTP status code; scripts/windows/webui-pilot/bridge.ps1 runs the shared hostile corpus in both argument positions plus malformed, non-object and oversized bodies and bad keys, requires the native ERR_TELEMETRY_REFUSED code for each (a synchronous throw, transport error or timeout fails), checks at the sink that ArdiaShell.testTelemetrySink's requestsStarted (counted where the request is handed to the network) stays 0, and sends a valid control that must reach a loopback listener with the same body and key; scripts/windows/engine/tests/webui_policy_test.cc unit-tests the shared telemetry policy

Windows WebUI host (--ardia-shell=webui): only the trusted shell document's ardiaRequest reaches ardia::desktop::Platform(); ArdiaApp.openExternalURL takes exactly one string and allows only http, https and mailto: the raw text may not hold whitespace, control characters, quotes or backslashes or exceed 32 KB, http(s) must be written scheme://host with no credentials, and only then does ShellExecuteExW see the canonical spec; a background instance opens nothing; setLaunchAtLogin takes one boolean and writes only HKCU Run 'Ardia WebUI' as the quoted executable path (refusing a path with quotes or control characters) plus --ardia-shell=webui, never RNW's 'Ardia' value; the default browser calls take no arguments and only open ms-settings:defaultapps, and platform.ps1 sends the shared corpus as one-item lists to setAsDefaultBrowser and checks the default apps launch count never moves until an empty-list control moves it by one; DPAPI secrets accept account names of 1-64 [A-Za-z0-9_-] only, are stored as sync-key-x<hex of the exact account bytes>.dpapi so accounts differing only by case never share a file on NTFS, live under the WebUI data folder's Sync, are bound to the ardia-sync-key/v1 purpose and instance, and are zeroed after use; scripts/windows/webui-pilot/platform.ps1 sends the shared hostile corpus (scripts/security/hostile-inputs.mjs via hostile-corpus.mjs) plus unlisted schemes and bad shapes to openExternalURL in a Windows guest and checks at the sink that the ShellExecuteExW count never moves, then that one https control moves it by one

A magnify event seen while another app is in front only resizes a Picture in Picture window: the monitor exists only while Ardia is inactive with a zoomable window, a missing CGEvent falls back to the mouse location, a non-finite or far-off pointer is refused before hit-testing, the window must be the topmost under the pointer, and a non-finite or huge magnification becomes a factor between 0.05 and 4 before the clamped, finite-checked resize

Background renderer efficiency counts kept by the Windows engine layer itself, asked for and kept per consent epoch; only whole positive numbers under the seven known keys are added, anything else counts as 0

Trace events describe what the page did: each field is type-checked and length-capped, event count capped at MAX_TRACE_EVENTS; only the inspected tab's main frame navigation, frames and renderer process count, bounded to the selected navigation; only numbers, enums and capped URLs reach the reply; nothing is stored
Audits issues are read field by field into a fixed shape; codes must be letters only; cookie names, domains and paths only, never the raw cookie line or value; capped at MAX_ISSUES
Matched styles are read into a fixed shape with capped strings, rule and inheritance counts; the selector goes to DOM.querySelector as data and property names must match a CSS identifier pattern

Source maps come only from what the caller passes (a map, its JSON, a data: URL, or a script's text whose inline data: map is read) or a script's own inline data: sourceMapURL from Debugger.scriptParsed; Ardia fetches nothing, so a page's sourceURL or sourceMappingURL can't make it reach the network. Size, section, line and segment counts capped; all logpoint sessions together keep at most MAX_HELD_MAP_BYTES of maps, each keeps at most MAX_HELD_FRAMES frames, and a navigated frame's scripts are dropped; mappings with a wrong segment length or a negative position, and negative section offsets, are refused

ardia-webui-migrate (ardia-shell-migration) reads the React Native Windows shell's data folder, config folder, sealed sync keys and Credential Manager items, which any same-user process could have planted or linked, and copies them once into the WebUI host's folder: names follow the RNW stores' own rules (document names, theme names, sync-key accounts) and accounts become lowercase hex file names; every root is walked from the volume root and every folder opened relative to a held handle without following links (openat, NtCreateFile with RootDirectory and FILE_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT), and writes, renames, deletes and the lock go through those handles, files with more than one link and oversized files are skipped; the shared hostile corpus runs through tests/hostile.rs and is checked at the filesystem sink, folders that overlap are refused, every write is staged and renamed, DPAPI runs with CRYPTPROTECT_UI_FORBIDDEN and plaintext is zeroed; the attempt report holds only enums and counts and the UI sends only known enums and capped counts from it

devtools.attach, send, batch and detach open a full DevTools client of one tab over the control socket for the owner's connection only (plugin sessions are refused by accessProblem; D3: any same-user process the socket let in is the owner, the same trust as control.devtoolsEndpoint's token). Params are checked against the method's schema, the tab through tabOf (private tabs never), the method name against METHOD_NAME, a child sessionId against CHILD_SESSION, params must be an object and a batch holds at most MAX_BATCH commands with only method, params and sessionId. Every engine session is an untrusted DevTools client (IsTrusted false, so Chromium gives it auto-attach only: no Target.getTargets, attachToTarget or createTarget), never attaches to a WebUI or chrome:// page (MayAttachToURL) or to any frame of an off-the-record profile (MayAttachToRenderFrameHost), so it can only reach its own tab and that tab's iframes and workers; at most 4000 events wait in the engine (the rest counted as dropped) and an event over the cap is cut from its prefix before it is parsed. A session belongs to its connection (ownedSession) and the engine checks the owner again (SessionFor); the engine refuses private tabs (CliTabRefusal), needs the RemoteDebuggingAllowed policy at open and at every command (revoking it ends every session at once) and IsInspectionAllowed for the tab, caps sessions (kMaxSessions, kMaxSessionsPerOwner), takes only ValidMethodName names, an inspect session only kInspectionMethods, and passes an event over 900 KiB as cut. Sessions end when their tab closes, the connection closes (closeEngineCliFor, CancelCliOps) or control goes off (CloseAllCliDevToolsSessions)

tabs.snapshot, waitSettled, hitTest, click and screenshot take the tab through tabOf, a ref only as e<digits>, a point only as finite numbers within 100000 CSS pixels (never with a ref), and limits within the schema's ranges; the engine reads them again (ReadTarget, ReadOwner, ScreenshotOptionsFromArgs), refuses private tabs and tabs DevTools policy keeps from inspection, caps each operation at 15 s (settle at the caller's timeout, at most 60 s), and calls it off when its connection closes (RegisterCliOp, CancelCliOps). A click goes through the same hit test and is held back while something covers the target unless force. Every entry point, screenshot included, refuses private tabs and needs the RemoteDebuggingAllowed policy and IsInspectionAllowed (CliTabRefusal); turning control off or revoking the policy cancels every running operation (CancelAllCliOps). A click is refused unless the hit test reached the target or something inside it, and is checked again after the pointer moves, so a layer that appears meanwhile stops it

The snapshot reads each frame's accessibility tree and layout from Chromium through the tab's own untrusted DevTools session (Accessibility.getFullAXTree, DOMSnapshot.captureSnapshot), never page script, frame by frame in frame-tree order, at most 24 frames, each refused frame (DevTools policy, private profile, WebUI: CliFrameRefused) left out with everything under it, at most kMaxItems nodes: names and values are cut to 200 bytes at a UTF-8 boundary (ClippedUtf8), at most maxRefs rows and maxTextBytes of text, at most 24 frames; the DevTools answers it uses for hit tests (DOM.getNodeForLocation, DOM.describeNode, Page.getLayoutMetrics) are read field by field with types checked and only map to nodes already in the tree (PageModel::Find), coordinates past a million pixels are dropped; dismiss buttons are chosen by fixed word lists (DismissChoices), nothing the page says is run or stored beyond the tab's ref table (RefStore, at most 4000 refs, cleared of node ids on navigation). A password field and an input whose autocomplete names a card, a one-time code or a password (split on every HTML whitespace) never has its value or the text under it listed (SensitiveAutocomplete; redacted: true). A ref rebinds only inside its own frame and only to the one element there with its role and name; a main-frame navigation forgets every ref

A screenshot is pixels copied from the tab's compositor surface (RenderWidgetHostView::CopyFromSurface) and encoded in the browser process on a worker thread; its size is capped at kMaxSide per side and kMaxPixels in all, the clip must be finite and within the page, and Page.captureScreenshot sent on a session is answered this way only for its own tab when it isn't on screen

Windows WebUI host (--ardia-shell=webui): documents.watch, unwatch, commit and flush arrive as engine.call from the live trusted chrome://ardia/ shell document only, for the app profile name "default" only, with JSON text of at most 8 MiB (DocumentEngineRequestAllowed) parsed in RFC mode to depth 48 as an object (ParseDocumentVerb picks the verb; anything else is ERR_DOCUMENT_REQUEST); a subscription names exactly {document: "live.json"}; a private window gets ERR_DOCUMENT_AUTH; the client id is scoped to the authority, the window and the renderer generation (EnsureDocumentClient) and is retired with the renderer; change events reach the shell only while the subscription sequence that asked for them is current (DocumentSubscription) and the authority scope still matches; the shared LinuxDocumentService from engine/ardiacore-linux validates every operation and reads and writes its envelope through ReadCanonicalDocument and WriteCanonicalEnvelope, capped at kLinuxLiveMaxBytes; scripts/windows/engine/tests/webui_window_policy_test.cc unit-tests the verb parser and the subscription sequence

Windows WebUI host (--ardia-shell=webui): ArdiaShell.openWindow, focusWindow and setActiveProfile come only from a live trusted shell document; a window id is 1-256 of [A-Za-z0-9._:-] (ValidWindowId), settings and import open only under their own id and no browser window may take those ids (ClassifyOpenWindow), a private seed needs incognito and a private profile name, utility windows are never private and a small-window seed only opens a non-private small window (OpenWindowProfileAllowed), seeds are capped at 64 KiB of JSON, at most 64 windows are open, a requested frame must be finite and is fitted to the display's work area (ValidRect, FitToWorkArea), a profile joins a window as a hidden companion browser only when neither side is private, a utility window or closing (RouteProfile), and setActiveProfile drops any selection older than the newest one for the same renderer (SelectionSequence); scripts/windows/engine/tests/webui_window_policy_test.cc unit-tests each rule; a window opens only for the shell document that asked: the request and the profile load that follows both check that this window's renderer generation is still the live one (LiveFor), so a reloaded or closed shell document cannot open a window late, and ArdiaShell.minimizeWindow names its target window by id through the registry; Chromium's Open link in private window (the taken chromium-linux-private-links hook) never opens a Chromium private window: OffTheRecordNavigation hands the link to the shell as an openWindow page event only for a tab a live shell document owns, naming a regular profile that passes PrivateLinkProfile, and refuses it otherwise; any other private window Chromium opens is hidden and its pages are offered the same way to the shell of the private window sharing its session or the front regular window, retried for 5 s, then moved into the same-session private window as unclaimed tabs (HandOverPrivateWindow, NextHandOverStep, OriginalProfileOf)

Windows WebUI host (--ardia-shell=webui): ArdiaShell.pickFolder takes at most a current folder and a button title, each a string or null; the title is used only when PickerPromptUsable accepts it (1-200 bytes of valid UTF-8 with no control characters) and the start folder only when absolute; pickFiles takes no arguments; one dialog per window at a time (ERR_PICKER_OPEN), refused when policy disables file choosers, and a background test instance answers null or [] without showing a dialog; ArdiaShell.copyText takes exactly one string that CopyTextFits (valid UTF-8 of at most 1 MiB), and readText returns the clipboard text cut to 1 MiB of UTF-8 bytes at a character boundary (TruncateUtf8), never UTF-16 units; scripts/windows/engine/tests/webui_window_policy_test.cc runs a hostile corpus (NULs, control characters, overlong and surrogate UTF-8, bidi overrides, path traversal, foreign schemes, oversized values) through each of these rules

Windows WebUI host (--ardia-shell=webui): a second launch of Ardia hands its command-line arguments to the running browser (WebUIRelaunched); WebUIRelaunchUrls keeps only arguments that parse as valid URLs (a relative file path is fixed up against the caller's folder first) whose scheme is http, https or file, each at most 32 KiB and at most 64 of them (RelaunchUrlAccepted); the registry queues them and delivers them only as ArdiaShell onOpenURLs to the most recently active browser window that is not private, not a utility window, not closing, and whose live shell document called ArdiaShell.listenForOpenURLs for its current renderer generation (DeliverOpenUrls, OpenUrlsListening); scripts/windows/engine/tests/webui_window_policy_test.cc runs the hostile corpus through the scheme and size rules

tabs.input params pass the method's closed schema, then checkedInput (tabInput.ts): one of eight actions with only that action's fields (clickCount on down and up only), finite coordinates within 0-100000, left or middle buttons (a right click or control-click would open Ardia's own menu), known modifiers (no control or meta on the wheel, which zooms), wheel deltas within ±10000, a key that is one printable character or a key name other than ContextMenu (or Shift+F10) and a code that is a key code, and well-formed NUL-free text of at most 4096 units; private and ineligible tabs are refused by tabOf. socketTabTools.test.mjs sends the shared hostile corpus over the socket in every field and checks what reaches the engine call (the sink): only checked shapes, or nothing; tabInput.test.mjs and hostileInputs.test.mjs run it through checkedInput directly. The engine checks again on its own (Build): the same per-action field list (Takes), private and crashed tabs, pages that aren't web pages (TakesInput), points outside the viewport (PointOf), keys it can't map or that open the context menu, NUL in key, code or text (KeyOf, Text), held-button transitions (a second down, an unmatched up, a click on a held button, and a down, up, click or dblclick while another is unanswered, which consumes its prime token and answers busy), present optional fields of the wrong type or value (button, clickCount, deltaX, deltaY, code, prime, token), more than four modifiers, coordinates above 100000, a token on a prime, and a send's prime token, which it spends before any other check so a refused send never holds one of its 16 slots, and a token binding the send to the documents prime saw (Dispatch); keys go with skip_if_unhandled (KeyEvent). packages/ardiacore/scripts/tab-tools-check.mjs exercises live, through the socket and one call at a time: the NUL refusals, out-of-viewport points, right clicks, the sequential held-button transitions (an unmatched up, a second down, a click on a held button), trusted delivery on a hidden background tab and the absence of any activation. No test sends overlapping presses, so the busy answer is unexercised. The engine's own copies of the field, NUL and context-menu checks sit behind the socket guard, so the corpus and the live run reach them only where the guard lets a value through

The engine records console messages and network requests only from the primary page of tabs that aren't private and that DevTools may inspect (Recordable), into fixed rings of 200 console and 250 network entries per tab freed with the tab, messages clipped to 1000 UTF-16 units and addresses cut to origin and path with no user, password, query or fragment (DiagnosticsUrl); no headers or bodies are kept. Before the socket, redactText and redactUrl replace tokens, keys, passwords, JWTs, private keys and secret-looking path segments with [redacted]
